Date: 2025-08-18

summary: Kickoff for contract acceptance and technical preflight. Legal raised a few DPA/egress questions and asked for explicit SLAs for dedicated capacity. Action items assigned for MSA redline, pilot checklist, and document exchange.
topics: DPA clauses: data residency, subprocessors, breach notification
SLA expectations for Dedicated capacity (p95/p99 latency targets, uptime)
Pricing approval paths and commitment tiers
Technical preflight: VPC peering, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM integration
Pilot scope and success criteria (throughput, latency, quality)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: OK everyone, thanks for joining. Uh this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Priya our SE. How are we all doing?
[00:08] Rajiv: Doing well, thanks. We wanted to get the contract finalization and technical preflight aligned. Maya is on from legal to cover DPA stuff.
[00:15] Maya: Hi all. Yes, quick note — we have a few non‑standard asks on data residency and the breach notification timelines.
[00:20] Priya: Great, we'll cover those. Ethan can you give a very short summary of what the platform team needs from us for the pilot?
[00:28] Ethan: Sure. We're mostly looking to validate 2 things: steady‑state throughput around 300 tokens/sec for our primary model, and 99th percentile latency under 350ms for conversational requests. Also need confirmation on VPC peering and SSO flows.
[00:42] Priya: Okay good, that's helpful. Just to set expectations from our side, Redwood has hosted, dedicated and private deployment modes. For this procurement lane you're evaluating dedicated — that gives predictable capacity and SLA options but there are some onboarding steps (VPC, KMS, CNI, et cetera).
[01:05] Maya: On the DPA side we need explicit subprocessor disclosures and a 72‑hour breach notification window. The standard DPA you sent had a 7 day window.
[01:15] Jordan: Understood, thanks for flagging. We can surface the SOC2 and DPA to you — I'm going to upload the latest SOC2 Type II and our subprocessor list after this call.
[01:27] Rajiv: Also pricing. Finance wants to know: if we commit to a 12 month reserved pool what's the price per GPU‑hour and what happens if we spike above committed throughput? Any overage rates?
[01:39] Priya: Yep. We'll share the dedicated capacity pricing matrix. There are commit tiers — e.g., 4x A100 equivalent reserved nodes gets X price, and burst capacity is available at Y rate. For overage we typically charge a blended overage per token and also provide burst credits depending on the contract. We'll send the concrete numbers.
[01:59] Ethan: Quick question — in terms of KMS, do you support customer‑managed keys or only Redwood keys? We need to ensure key separation on the dedicated cluster.
[02:09] Priya: For Dedicated we support BYOK via KMS integrations — we can integrate with your cloud KMS and support key rotation policies. For Private on‑prem we support HSMs too but that has a separate onboarding timeline.
[02:25] Maya: Any SLA language around key management you provide? Like responsibility for key compromise?
[02:31] Jordan: Typically the MSA allocates responsibility — Redwood manages platform controls, you manage key access credentials. We can add explicit language about KMS boundaries. We'll propose redline language.
[02:45] Rajiv: On egress — our legal wants an egress cap and clarity on data persistence. We can't accept indefinite retention of prompts or customer data unless it's hashed/ephemeral or under DPA terms.
[02:58] Priya: We have configurable retention policies. Hosted API has default retention for X days, but Dedicated can be configured to not persist user prompts beyond session, and we can log things to your logging stack as needed. We'll clarify in the DPA.
[03:15] Maya: Also subprocessors — please provide the full subprocessor list. We need to know if any third party is in a different jurisdiction.
[03:22] Jordan: I'll upload the current subprocessor list and confirm jurisdictions in the follow up.
[03:28] Ethan: Network question — do we require NAT egress if the dedicated cluster sits in our VPC, or do you do VPC peering? What are the typical architecture patterns?
[03:39] Priya: Typical approach is VPC peering for Dedicated, with optional PrivateLink. We also support customer‑managed NAT egress if you prefer. We'll include network diagrams in the pilot checklist.
[03:52] Rajiv: And what's the typical lead time to provision dedicated capacity? Finance wants dates.
[03:58] Priya: Depends on region and commit size — usually 2–4 weeks after contract signature for standard configurations, maybe longer for specialized HSM or air‑gapped setups. We can commit to a target in the SLA if needed.
[04:12] Maya: On the MSA I'm seeing one clause about escrow that we may want to expand — if Redwood materially changes pricing we want a pathway for exit or price protections.
[04:22] Jordan: We can propose language for price protection windows and an escrow fallback if there are material discontinuities. Good to capture that in the redline.
[04:31] Rajiv: Regarding SLAs — we need p95 and p99 latency commitments plus uptime and an SLA credit mechanism. Can you commit to p99 numbers for the dedicated tier?
[04:41] Priya: Yes, for dedicated we provide an SLA with uptime and latency SLOs; p99 depends on model size and sequence length but we can profile with your real traffic during the pilot and then publish an SLO tied to that configuration.
[04:56] Ethan: Will there be a fallback model if the dedicated pool is saturated? We don't want production outages.
[05:02] Priya: We can define an automatic fallback policy to a lower‑cost/compatible model or route requests to burst capacity. We'll document that as part of rollout policy.
[05:12] Maya: On change of control and assignment clauses — we need assurance that any transfer of rights won't expose our data to unauthorized parties.
[05:20] Jordan: Standard MSA language covers assignment, but we can add specific assurances about subcontractor transfers and continued obligations in case of acquisition. We'll flag that for legal redline.
[05:31] Rajiv: Good. On pricing approvals, our procurement team needs two alternatives: 12 month commit and a pilot / short term trial pricing. Can you provide both?
[05:41] Jordan: Yes we'll provide an option with 12 month commit discounts and a pilot pricing for a 30 day reserved test.
[05:47] Ethan: For the pilot we need a reproducible test harness. What telemetry do you export? Token counts, latency histograms, per‑route cost?
[05:56] Priya: We export token-level usage, latency percentiles, error rates, and model-specific cost breakdown. The Redwood Console can break down by API key and model. We'll provide documented endpoints for the pilot to pull telemetry.
[06:12] Rajiv: Security checklist — SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, penetration testing reports. We will need weekly access to audit logs during the pilot.
[06:23] Priya: Audit logs can be forwarded to your logging infrastructure or stored in our console with retention. For dedicated we'll typically forward logs to your SIEM. We'll include PT reports and SOC2 in the package.
[06:36] Maya: On the DPA breach window — you said you could shorten it from 7 days to 72 hours?
[06:41] Jordan: I'll confirm with security but we believe 72 hours for critical incidents is achievable; we'll include the proposed language in the redline. If there's a need for split notification (e.g., 24 hours for confirmed breach), we'll call that out.
[06:55] Ethan: Is there any restriction on using model weights or telemetry for model improvement? We can't have customer prompts used to train public models.
[07:03] Priya: We have explicit terms: data used for modeling improvements is opt‑in. For dedicated deployments we do not use customer prompts for training unless explicitly contracted. We'll add that to the DPA.
[07:20] Rajiv: Great. On the legal schedule — what's realistic for turnaround on the redline? Our counsel needs a week to review.
[07:26] Maya: If you can get redlines to us by Friday we'll review and iterate. A week turnaround should be fine.
[07:31] Jordan: We'll aim to send annotated redline by Friday, 2025-08-22.
[07:36] Priya: For the pilot, let's schedule a 1 hour network + runbook session the week after redline is shared. Ethan, do mornings or afternoons work better?
[07:44] Ethan: Mornings are better for us.
[07:46] Priya: Great, we'll send a Doodle.
[07:49] Rajiv: A few nitty gritty questions — for pricing transparency we want line items for GPU cost, licensing, and a service fee. Can you provide a breakdown?
[07:58] Jordan: Yes — we'll send a line‑item quote showing compute, storage, and platform fee plus any optional add ons like extended retention and premium SLAs.
[08:08] Maya: Also, regarding subcontractor jurisdiction — any subprocessor in EMEA vs US vs APAC needs to be highlighted. We have specific controls for EU data.
[08:16] Jordan: We'll call out subprocessors and their jurisdictions in the follow up.
[08:21] Priya: Technical note — when we run the pilot we'll include a KV cache warmup plan; many vendors see initial cold penalty. We'll set expectations for the first N minutes of load.
[08:34] Ethan: Good point. We'll include our warmup traffic pattern in the test plan.
[08:38] Maya: On indemnity — we're looking for mutual indemnity with a carve‑out for willful misconduct.
[08:45] Jordan: Mutual indemnity with standard caps is typical — we'll propose language and highlight any exceptions.
[08:51] Rajiv: About termination for convenience — we want a short notice period for proofs of concept. Can that be 30 days?
[08:58] Jordan: For pilot/trial 30 days is standard. For long term committed contracts it's usually 90 days, but we can be explicit in the MSA.
[09:09] Ethan: Networking again — when peering, do you terminate TLS at your side or can we provide our own TLS certs? We need mutual TLS for some endpoints.
[09:19] Priya: We support mTLS on dedicated endpoints, you can provide certs and we can rotate keys per your policy. We'll document the steps.
[09:29] Maya: Do you perform background penetration tests and will you share results under NDA?
[09:35] Jordan: Yes, we perform regular pen tests and can share high‑level reports under NDA. We'll put the summary in the security pack.
[09:44] Rajiv: Any precedence with other fintechs using dedicated? We want references for regulated workloads.
[09:51] Jordan: We have several customers in payments and SMB financial services on dedicated with similar constraints — I can provide anonymized references and case studies.
[09:59] Priya: Also, for latency profiling we can run a synthetic and replay of your sample traffic. We will need your sample traces.
[10:08] Ethan: We'll export traces and spike scenarios — will send via secure file share.
[10:12] Jordan: Perfect. So next steps recap: Jordan uploads SOC2 and DPA drafts; Jordan sends MSA redline by Friday; Priya shares pricing and pilot matrix; Priya/Ethan schedule pilot runbook session next week mornings; Maya to provide legal must‑haves; Ethan to share traffic profile. Anything else?
[10:28] Maya: One more — indemnity and jurisdiction clause, we prefer state of New York or Delaware, we'll flag in redline.
[10:36] Jordan: Noted, will include jurisdiction options.
[10:39] Rajiv: That's about it from procurement. If legal signs off quickly we can aim for provisioning in 2–4 weeks.
[10:46] Priya: All right — we'll follow up with the package. Thanks everyone.
[10:50] Jordan: Thanks, we'll send the materials. End of call.
